identity.title: Physics of ULIRGs with MUSE and ALMA: The PUMA project. IV. No tight relation between cold molecular outflow rates and AGN luminosities

paper_type_evidence.quote: We study molecular outflows in a sample of 25 nearby ( _z_ < 0.17, _d_ < 750 Mpc) ultra-luminous infrared galaxy (ULIRG) systems (38 individual nuclei) as part of the Physics of ULIRGs with MUSE and ALMA (PUMA) survey, using ∼ 400 pc (0.1-1.0" beam FWHM) resolution ALMA CO(2-1) observations.
In this work, we analyse ALMA 12-m array CO(2-1) 230.538 GHz observations of the 25 ULIRGs systems in the PUMA sample.

question.value: Determine the prevalence, properties, driving mechanisms (starburst vs. AGN, momentum- vs. energy-driven), and feedback effects of spatially resolved cold molecular outflows in nearby ULIRGs, and compare CO(2-1) outflow properties with OH 119 um outflow signatures.

evidence.quote: In this work, we present high spatial resolution (0.1-1.0", ∼ 400 pc) ALMA observations of the CO(2-1) line for an unbiased sample of 25 ULIRGs, selected only based on their IR luminosity.

The main goals of PUMA are the following: (i) to study the prevalence of outflows in different gas phases (ionised, neutral, and molecular) as a function of the galaxy properties, (ii) to determine the driving mechanisms of the outflows
In Section 5.4, we compare the outflow properties derived from the CO(2-1) data with the ones derived from the OH 119 µm doublet.

claims.hypothesis: Cold molecular mass outflow rates and mass-loading factors in ULIRGs correlate tightly with AGN luminosity and AGN fraction as reported in earlier literature.
claims.experiment: Measure spatially resolved CO(2-1) mass outflow rates and mass-loading factors across an unbiased sample of 25 ULIRG systems (38 nuclei) selected only by IR luminosity, and compare with MIR/optical AGN fractions and AGN luminosities.
claims.result: No correlation is found between mass-loading factor eta and AGN fraction alpha_AGN (Spearman r = 0.27, p = 0.28), and M_dot_out spans up to 1.2 dex at a given AGN luminosity, lying below the Cicone et al. (2014) relation.
claims.finding: ULIRGs do not follow a tight M_dot_out vs L_AGN relation; previous scaling relations likely trace only the upper boundary of the most extreme outflows.

evidence.quote: Cicone et al. (2014) reported a trend for the mass-loading factor (η = _M_ [˙] _out_ /SFR) to increase with AGN fraction (α _AGN_ = _L_ _AGN_ / _L_ _bol_ ), while we do not find a correlation between these two quantities in our sample (Spearmann rank correlation coefficient for the detections _r_ = 0.27, _p_ -value=0.28)

We find that our sample does not follow a tight _M_ [˙] _out_ versus AGN luminosity relation, as reported in previous works (see Fig. 16). For the same AGN luminosity, we find _M_ [˙] _out_ spanning up to 1.2 dex.

claims.hypothesis: Cold molecular outflow detection rates and orientations in ULIRGs depend on the dominant nuclear power source (starburst vs AGN) and merger stage.
claims.experiment: Perform spectro-astrometry on ALMA CO(2-1) cubes for 26 ULIRG nuclei with log L_IR/L_sun > 11.8 to detect decoupled high-velocity (>300 km s^-1) gas and measure its projected angle relative to the kinematic major axis.
claims.result: Outflows are detected in 93 +- 4% (14/15) of SB nuclei versus 55 +- 14% (6/11) of AGN nuclei; 6/14 SB outflows are perpendicular to the kinematic major axis (5/6 in interacting SBs), whereas AGN outflows show no preferred orientation.
claims.finding: Outflow detection rates are higher in starbursts than in AGN, and perpendicular outflows occur mainly in interacting starbursts, likely because SB outflows follow the path of least resistance perpendicular to the disk while AGN outflows can have any orientation or be compact.

evidence.quote: The percentage of detections in SB (93 ± 4%, 14/15) is higher than in AGN (55 ± 14%, 6/11).

Indeed, we find that in 43% (6/14) of the SB nuclei with outflow detection, the projected position angle of the outflow is along the kinematic minor axis, which suggests that these outflows are perpendicular to the disk. This fraction is higher in early interacting SBs (50%) than in advanced merger SBs (17%).

claims.hypothesis: Cold molecular outflows in ULIRGs and nearby star-forming galaxies are momentum-driven rather than energy-driven.
claims.experiment: Combine the PUMA ULIRG sample with the PHANGS-ALMA main-sequence outflow sample to fit the scaling relations between v_out, SFR, eta, and M_out/R_out using MCMC bisector regression.
claims.result: v_out correlates with SFR as v_out propto SFR^(0.25 +- 0.01) (r = 0.84, p < 0.01); using this relation, log(M_out/R_out) vs log v_out has a slope of 2.61 +- 0.25, corresponding to alpha = -0.39 +- 0.25 in eta propto v_out^alpha, consistent within 1 sigma with momentum-driven (alpha = -1) and inconsistent with energy-driven (alpha = -2). Also, outflow momentum rates are all below total SNe momentum injection.
claims.finding: The molecular outflows are consistent with being momentum-driven and can be powered by supernovae.

evidence.quote: Therefore, our analysis favours the momentum-driven scenario as the primary launching mechanism for molecular outflows in ULIRGs.

claims.hypothesis: CO(2-1) emission and OH 119 um absorption/emission trace the same molecular outflow velocities.
claims.experiment: Fit archival Herschel/PACS OH 119 um doublet profiles for 22 PUMA systems to derive v_98 percentile velocities and compare with CO(2-1) outflow velocities (v_out and v_max).
claims.result: Among 17 targets with outflow detections in at least one tracer (out of 20 nuclei with OH absorption/P-Cygni), 13 (76%) show outflows in both CO and OH (|v| > 300 km s^-1), 3 (18%) show outflows only in CO, and 1 (00188-0856) shows an outflow only in OH; |v_98(OH) - v_max(CO)| anti-correlates weakly with R_out (r = -0.4) and correlates with alpha_AGN (r = 0.51).
claims.finding: CO and OH detect the same outflow in most targets, but velocity discrepancies arise because OH absorption requires a far-IR continuum background, making it sensitive to outflow collimation and geometry, or extreme ionisation lowering CO abundance.

evidence.quote: In 76% of the targets, the outflow is detected in both CO and OH, while in three targets (18%) the outflow is only detected in CO, and in one target the outflow is detected in OH but not in CO. The difference between the OH and CO outflow velocities could be due to the far-IR background source required by the OH absorption which makes these observations more dependent on the specific outflow geometry.

We find a weak anti-correlation between the _R_ _out_ and the OH-CO velocity difference ( _r_ = −0.4, or _r_ = −0.3 if we exclude the point with _v_ _max_ (CO)=0 km s [−][1] ), meaning that for more extended CO outflow, the CO velocity tend to be larger than the OH velocity.

why_this_data.value: High spatial resolution (~400 pc) ALMA CO(2-1) observations of an unbiased, IR-luminosity-selected sample of 25 ULIRGs are needed to spatially resolve outflow radii and avoid the bias toward extreme outflows present in prior pre-selected samples; PHANGS-ALMA is added to increase the L_IR/SFR dynamic range.

evidence.quote: In most cases, the targeted objects were selected based on the presence of an outflow, which was detected through previous low-resolution observations. This could introduce a bias in the samples, in which only ULIRGs with the most-extreme outflows are selected. In this work, we present high spatial resolution (0.1-1.0", ∼ 400 pc) ALMA observations of the CO(2-1) line for an unbiased sample of 25 ULIRGs, selected only based on their IR luminosity.

In our analysis, we include a sample of nearby main-sequence galaxies (SFR = 0.3 − 17 M ⊙ yr [−][1] ) with detected molecular outflows from the PHANGS-ALMA survey to increase the _L_ _IR_ dynamic range.

why_this_method.value: Spectro-astrometry and integration of only high-velocity (|v| > 300 km s^-1) flux-weighted channels avoids the strong parameter degeneracies of multi-Gaussian fitting to asymmetric/self-absorbed line cores; fitting M_out/R_out vs v_out using the v_out-SFR relation reduces scatter compared to fitting eta vs v_out directly.
